desc:
The array nums is sorted in non-decreasing order. Delete every element whose value occurs more than once (all of its copies, not just the extra ones) and return what is left, in order.

nums = [1, 2, 2, 3, 4, 4, 4, 5]
result = [1, 3, 5]
nums = [7, 7, 7]
result = []

Use O(1) extra space apart from the returned array.
constraints: nums is sorted in non-decreasing order
hints: Equal values form contiguous runs. A value survives only if its run has length exactly 1.
A value at index i is unique when it differs from both its left neighbour and its right neighbour (a missing neighbour counts as different).
Walk i through the array with a write pointer. Copy nums[i] to nums[write] only if nums[i] != nums[i - 1] and nums[i] != nums[i + 1] (checking bounds).
editorial: Because the array is sorted, a repeated value must be adjacent to one of its copies. Therefore an element is a single exactly when it is different from the element before it and from the element after it. This turns the problem into a filter with a local test.

Run a read index over the array and compact the survivors with a write pointer, just like in the usual removal of duplicates. Do not overwrite values that you still have to look at: since write ≤ read and you only ever need nums[i - 1], keep the previous original value in a variable (or read from the untouched copy) instead of from the partially overwritten array.
A single pass gives O(n) time and O(1) extra space.
solution:
def keepSingles(nums):
    a = list(nums)
    n = len(a)
    w = 0
    prev = None
    for i in range(n):
        x = a[i]
        nxt = a[i + 1] if i + 1 < n else None
        if n and x != prev and x != nxt:
            a[w] = x
            w += 1
        prev = x
    return a[:w]
